meta.title: Customer interview — meeting copilot
meta.product_context: Live conversation copilot with real-time transcription and suggestion cards

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Hi Morgan, thanks for making time. I'm Pavel, product manager on a tool we're calling the meeting copilot. Is it okay if I use this call for product discovery? Nothing gets shared outside our team without your consent.

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Yes, that's fine. Happy to help. I've been curious about tools in this space anyway.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Great. I'd love to start with your world. What does a typical customer interview look like for you — from before the call through what happens after you hang up?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Sure. I run about four to six interviews a week for a B2B workflow product — mostly PMs and ops leads. Before the call I pull a discussion guide in Google Docs. During the call I'm on Zoom with Otter transcribing in the background. I'm trying to listen, ask follow-ups, and jot notes at the same time, and that's the part that breaks down.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: When it breaks down, what's the first thing you lose — the thread, the notes, or something else?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: The follow-up thread. Someone mentions a workaround they've used for months, I think I'll come back to it, the conversation moves on, and twenty minutes later I've lost the moment. After the call I skim Otter and find three questions I wish I'd asked while we were still talking.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: How long does the post-call synthesis take you per interview?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Roughly forty-five minutes to an hour. Highlighting quotes, tagging needs in Dovetail, updating our research board. Rich sessions run longer. It's valuable work, but it's all reactive — I'm reconstructing what I missed live.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Have you tried anything that helps during the call itself, not just transcription afterward?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: I tried Granola briefly. Interesting, but it felt like another chat window dumping text while I'm trying to stay present on camera. I turned most of it off. Teams Copilot is more summary-after-the-fact — doesn't help me in the moment.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Let me describe what we're building and you can react. You pick a mode like customer interview. Main area is a stable two-by-two grid of cards — follow-up questions, customer needs, risks, topics to explore. Not a chat stream. Transcript on the right, about a quarter of the screen. Cards update live: short items, one-line rationale underneath. You discard, pin, or mark done without leaving the call.

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: The stable grid is already different from what I didn't like about Granola. I want to know where to look. If cards stay in the same place every session, I could build a habit instead of hunting for the latest AI paragraph.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: What would make you distrust it or turn it off mid-interview?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Noise. If a new bullet appears every few seconds and it's the same idea rephrased, I'll ignore the product. Also anything that yanks my scroll at the wrong time. If I discard something, it should stay gone unless the participant actually brings that thread back with new evidence.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: We spec semantic dedupe and limited resurfacing for exactly that. Does that match your bar?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: If it works, yes. I've had tools suggest 'ask about pricing' four times because someone said budget once. That's worse than no suggestion.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Are those four card types right for your interviews, or would you rearrange them?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Follow-up questions and customer needs are non-negotiable. Risks less often in pure research, more in discovery calls. I'd want custom modes — swap in jobs-to-be-done and unmet needs — without rebuilding the whole UI. One research study shouldn't fight the default template.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: What would you want to set before the session starts?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Interview goal, participant segment, hypothesis I'm testing. If suggestions ignore that and stay generic, I wouldn't open the app. Context can't be an afterthought.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: You saw a short Loom of the prototype — what landed, and what felt off?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Transcript on the right felt right — main area for action. Rationale under each item is what would make me trust a suggestion; otherwise it's vibes. Auto-scroll with a back-to-live when I scroll up — essential. I'd want keyboard shortcuts for pin and discard. I can't mouse around during a live interview.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: Anything in that prototype that felt unfinished?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Post-call was clearly TBD, and that's where I live. Pin and discard need to show up in a breakdown — what I kept, what I rejected — with export to Notion or Dovetail. Also four cards on a thirteen-inch laptop next to Zoom is tight; I'd need a compact layout.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: How do you think about privacy when customer audio is involved?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Deal-breaker territory. Clear consent, retention policy, and ideally clarity on whether audio leaves the device. Enterprise participants ask. If you say real-time AI, they assume cloud processing — you need to be explicit.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: If we shipped one thing in the next month, what would actually move the needle for you?

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Reliable follow-up question cards with low noise. Second is session export that respects pins versus discards. I don't need a novel — I need fewer missed threads in the forty-five minutes that matter.

segments.speaker: pm
segments.text: That's incredibly helpful. I'll follow up with a summary — and we'd love you on a replay demo when the UX build is ready. Thanks Morgan.

segments.speaker: customer
segments.text: Happy to test it. Good luck with the build.
